title: Immutable slots
blurb: Reading a tuple slot is fine; assigning to one raises TypeError. Rebinding the name builds a new tuple.

notes.1: A tuple of three values. Its slots are fixed once created.
notes.2: Indexing only reads – x gets 20 and t is untouched.
notes.3: t + (40,) builds a BRAND-NEW tuple and the name t is moved to it. The old tuple was never changed.
notes.4: Assigning into a slot is not allowed – tuples have no item assignment.

title: A list inside a tuple
blurb: The tuple's slots are fixed, but a slot that points to a list lets that list change.

notes.1: Slot 0 holds 1; slot 1 holds a REFERENCE to a separate list [2, 3].
notes.2: t[1] fetches the list and append changes the list itself. The tuple's slot still points to the same list.
notes.3: The tuple now prints with the 4 inside – the list changed, the tuple did not.
notes.4: Replacing the slot itself is forbidden – that would change the tuple.

title: Reverse slicing t1[4:0:-1]
blurb: A negative step walks from start leftwards and stops BEFORE stop.

notes.1: Seven values: index 0 is 3, index 4 is 15, index 6 is 21.
notes.2: An empty tuple to collect the picked values.
notes.3: range(4, 0, -1) gives 4, 3, 2, 1 – exactly the indexes t1[4:0:-1] visits. 0 is the stop, so it is excluded.
notes.4: Tuples can't grow, so each pick builds a NEW tuple: old res + a one-element tuple.
notes.6: The slice gives the same result in one expression.

title: + and * build new tuples
blurb: Concatenation and repetition never modify a tuple – they return a new one.

notes.3: + joins both into a third, new tuple. t1 and t2 are unchanged.
notes.4: * 3 repeats t1's values three times in a new tuple.
notes.5: += on a tuple is t1 = t1 + (5,): a new tuple is built and t1 is rebound to it.
notes.6: t3 still holds the old (1, 2, 3, 4) – it was built before t1 changed.

title: Packing and unpacking
blurb: Commas pack values into a tuple; assignment to several names unpacks them – counts must match.

notes.1: No parentheses needed: the commas pack three values into a tuple.
notes.2: Three names, three values: a gets 10, b gets 20, c gets 30.
notes.3: The right side packs (b, a) = (20, 10) first, then unpacks into a, b – a swap with no temp variable.
notes.4: Two names but three values – Python refuses.

title: Starred unpacking
blurb: A *name collects whatever the plain names don't take – always into a LIST.

notes.2: a takes the first, c takes the last, *b collects the middle three into a list.
notes.3: b takes the last value; *a collects the rest into a list.
notes.4: a and b take the first two; *c gets the remaining three.
notes.5: Nothing is left for *d, so it becomes an empty list – that's allowed.
notes.6: Three plain names need at least three values; two is not enough.
